items.title: 'Eternity of pain': Angus Taylor issues warning to Australians voting for One Nation
items.description: In his strongest remarks pushing back on One Nation, the opposition leader has accused the right-wing party of being a "column of smoke".

items.title: Footage shows interceptor missile test in Australian outback

items.title: Welsh pop singer Bonnie Tyler dies aged 75
items.description: Welsh pop singer Bonnie Tyler, ​famed for 1980s power ballads such as Total Eclipse of the ​Heart and Holding Out ​for a Hero, has died.

items.title: When politics becomes content the risks multiply
items.description: Every press conference, reel and podcast is now a chance for politicians to connect with voters. Yet the strategy that broadens an MP's reach can also amplify their biggest mistakes.

items.title: As the ceasefire cracks, Iran gets 'a complete reset' of pressure on its oil trade

items.title: India a 'top-tier' security partner for Australia as nations deepen defence ties

items.title: Death on day of Telstra outage investigated by police
items.description: Police in SA are investigating a death at a regional South Australian hospital yesterday, after Liberal Senator Kerrynne Liddle said an elderly person had died during the Telstra outage.

items.title: 'Bad mistake': ABC's editorial director questioned over inaccurate report

items.title: State of Origin decider breaks broadcast record

items.title: Family desperate for information on missing Queensland mother

items.title: 'Pretty cool': Trump announces win for Ukraine amid fiery NATO meeting
items.description: Donald Trump says his country will probably continue to attack Iran and says Ukraine will be given permission to manufacture much-needed Patriot missiles as it fights Russia's full-scale invasion.

items.title: This Place: Koala Brother, Yarriabini
items.description: Uncle Micklo Jarrett is a Gumbaynggirr man, sharing a dreamtime story about how Yarriabini mountain, on the mid north coast of New South Wales, got its name. As part of NAIDOC Week the ABC is looking at Indigenous peoples' connection to country, and what makes it so special. NAIDOC Week is marking 50 years of Deadly and runs from July 5 until July 12.

items.title: The grief of childlessness will always be with me
items.description: The grief of losing the chance to have baby is something I expect to carry forever. But I'm becoming more comfortable with the unconventional life I'm building with my partner April.

items.title: Cultural hub in Tennant Creek celebrates Warumungu culture for NAIDOC
items.description: Hundreds of people walked through the streets of Tennant Creek today as part of a NAIDOC march, finishing at the official reopening of the town's major First Nations cultural hub.

items.title: Three NT corrections officers stood down with pay over prisoner escape
items.description: Three Northern Territory corrections officers have been stood down with pay over a prisoner escape during a hospital transfer, which sparked a more than 48-hour manhunt earlier this week.

items.title: Children's commissioner quits as CLP set to pass controversial welfare changes

items.title: Gout Gout ruled out of World Under-20 athletics titles after training injury

items.title: 'He gave us 10 extra years': Australian-first immune centre opens in Canberra
items.description: The Centre for Personalised Medicine at Canberra Hospital uses cutting-edge technology to identify the causes of complex immune conditions to tailor treatments for patients.

items.title: Court told former Wagga Wagga MP was 'kept in dark' over visa scheme

items.title: The key ingredient keeping the snow season alive

items.title: Water in the air an 'untapped water resource' until now
items.description: Can water be made from air in WA's Wheatbelt? Researchers are putting an invention to the test.
